title: Mummies
summary: The Reborn: people for whom death does not last.

claims.text: Mummies die, spend a time in the Underworld, and come back to bodies that have healed.
Mummies are also called the Reborn, and not all of them are Egyptian.
A mummy's First Life was a mortal life in ancient Egypt; its end is the First Death.
True Death is the final end, from which no mummy returns.

title: The Spell of Life
summary: The Great Rite that makes mummies.

claims.text: The Great Rite, Rite of Rebirth and Spell of Life are one magical formula that creates mummies.
Horus claims the Rite was always tightly controlled, but its history says otherwise.
At first Horus and the high priest of the cult of Isis chose who would receive it, judging virtue and conviction.
Variants exist: the Cabiri of Europe and Asia Minor come from one, and the Bane Rite makes Bane Mummies.
The Shemsu-heru follow Horus's lead and keep the Code of Horus.
Horus laid down the Code during the crusade to restore Maat.
Their generals each died briefly to be Reborn, so the Osirian League was never without leaders.
Viziers run the Shemsu-heru as prime ministers, each over a different region.
The Sebayet are teachings on the origins and aims of the Shemsu-heru.

title: Ishmaelites
summary: Egyptian mummies who have left the Code of Horus.

claims.text: Ishmaelites are renegade Egyptian mummies who have turned from the Code of Horus.

title: Set and the Enemies of Horus
summary: The Antediluvian who slew Osiris, and those who serve Set.

claims.text: The first enemy of the Shemsu-heru was Set, the Antediluvian vampire who destroyed Osiris and sought to rule Egypt.
Set's many followers included the Setites, Set's own vampire progeny.

title: Children of Apophis
summary: Bane Mummies, servants of the Great Serpent.

claims.text: The Children of Apophis, or Bane Mummies, are made by a perverted form of the Great Rite.
Once minions of Set, they now serve the demonic force called Apophis.

title: Apophis
summary: The Great Serpent that would swallow the Sun.

claims.text: Apophis is the Great Serpent that threatens to devour the Sun, akin to the Wyrm of the Garou.
Apophis lies coiled around the world.
Maat is the order and balance of the cosmos; some hold that it has been overthrown.
In the afterlife the heart was weighed against the feather of Maat to judge the dead.

title: The Parts of the Soul
summary: How the Egyptians, and the Reborn, divide a person.

claims.text: The Ab is the heart, seat of consciousness and of good and evil.
The Ba travels to the Underworld and must return to the body for Rebirth; it is also an energy that fuels that work.
The Ka stays near the tomb to guard the body, or khat, and is also an energy.
The Khaibit is the shadow, close kin to the Ka; a mummy whose humanity is lost is ruled by it.
The Khu is an intangible shining veil over the body, and the Sahu is the eternal spiritual body.
The Ren, or True Name, is a vital part of the self that cannot be parted from the soul.

title: Names Among the Reborn
summary: True Names, Known Names and Use-Names.

claims.text: A mummy's Known Name is the name from First Life by which other mummies still know it.
A Use-Name is an alias taken to avoid notice.
Ren-hekau, the highest Hekau, gives power over things through their true names.
Sekhem is power or vital force, somewhat like the Chinese idea of Chi.
Sekhem, Ba and Ka are the traits of magic, death and rebirth.

title: Hekau
summary: The Egyptian magic of words of power.

claims.text: Hekau means words of power and was part of everyday Egyptian life.
Mummies alone still practise it, and more strongly than mortals did.
Its paths are Amulets, Alchemy, Celestial, Necromancy, Ren-hekau and Ushabti, each running from small cantrips to great sorcery.
Amulets makes magic items; Alchemy makes potions and drugs; Celestial rules stars and weather; Necromancy gives power over and among the dead; Ushabti animates figures.

title: Duat and Amenti
summary: The Underworld, and the hidden stronghold of the Egyptian dead.

claims.text: Duat is the Underworld, home of the Restless Dead, where mummies go between lives.
Amenti is the stronghold of the Egyptian dead, hidden in the Underworld.
The first Egyptian wraiths trapped in Duat could not tell whether this bleak state was the eternity they had been judged worthy of.
